then.text: The Silk Museum does a ghost tour for Halloween. The ghost is mostly Derek in a sheet. He's very committed.
A silk scarf makes a lovely present. I say that every year, and every year I get socks.
The trees have gone the colour of the old silk dyes. Very on brand, Macclesfield.

silk_fan.text: Macclesfield made silk buttons, then silk everything.
The mill's still standing. It just makes opinions now.

then.text: Watched the fireworks from the top of the 108 Steps. Lost count of the steps. And the fireworks.
Frost on the 108 Steps this morning. Counted them on my backside. Still not 108.
Wet steps today, so I'm counting them slowly. Still getting a different answer.
Can't see the top of the 108 Steps in this fog. Could be 200 of them now.
Last count of the day. If it comes out at 108, I'm retiring.

steps_man.text: Those are the 108 Steps. I've counted them four times.
I got a different number every time. I blame the steps.

then.text: The pigeons are sheltering under the Town Hall porch. Union rules: no flying in drizzle.
Up early? So are the pigeons. They clock on at sunrise and expect breakfast.
{greeting} Don't feed the pigeons. They've got a union.
Last week they held a work-to-rule outside the Town Hall.

else.text: Ooh, you've got a creature! Then you'll be wanting the noticeboard. There, by the stalls.
Folk pin up odd jobs. The Forest Rangers want their rabbits counted again. Catch one in the Forest and you're paid on the spot.
Help out enough and people start to know you. I'm known. Mostly by the pigeons.

else.text: {greeting} Don't feed the pigeons. They've got a union.
Last week they held a work-to-rule outside the Town Hall.

then.text: Halloween forecast: a ninety per cent chance of somebody's dad in a bedsheet. Scattered sweet wrappers by midnight.
Remember, remember, the fifth of November. I never do. I just follow the smell of burnt sausages.
White Christmas in Macc? I forecast it every year. Statistically, I'm due.
Leaves are turning. Gold, orange, russet. Then brown, then soggy, then in my gutters.
Frost likely. Or as we call it in Macc, drizzle that's made an effort.
Drizzle! Told you. I also told you sun, but let's focus on the bit I got right.
Sunshine in Macc! Write it down, nobody back home will believe you.
Fog this thick, I can't see the hills. I'm forecasting them anyway.

weather_man.text: {greeting} It'll rain by lunchtime. Or sun. Or both.
That's Macclesfield. We have all four seasons before breakfast.

jogger_flav.text: I do a lap of the town every morning!
Uphill both ways. Don't ask how. Macclesfield geometry.

hiker_flav.text: East is the Forest. Pines, pools and a lot of herons.
If a heron looks at you, look away. It's never about you.

then.text: Sun on the Bollin! The ducks are out sunbathing like they've paid for deckchairs.
The ducks are tucking in for the night. They do it in order of importance.

bank_ducks.text: The Bollin is lovely this time of year.
The ducks think they own it. Frankly, they might.

gate.text: We're rehearsing the Bollin Stomp. We need the whole road.
You'll want a creature before you head into the Forest, you know.
Pop in to see Professor Garside. She's by the east end, in the Field Station.

potteries_gate.text: Whoa there! Mind the ewes. I'm walking this lot down the lane to the top field and they've no road sense whatsoever.
Oh, it's you, love! I'm helping with the sheep. Your mum says you're off adventuring soon.
Get a creature from Professor Garside and show that Kit what for at the Field Station first. The lane'll be clear by then, and the Roaches aren't going anywhere.

macc_bowler.text: Welcome to the club. Flat shoes only, and the kettle is for members. You can be a member for the afternoon.
